stories.title: Deloitte releases Finnish sustainability reporting benchmark
stories.summary: Deloitte Finland has published its second benchmarking report on the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive. The study examines how 22 large and listed Finnish companies are navigating evolving regulatory landscapes and building on their initial experience with formal sustainability reporting. The reporting cycle continues to mature.

stories.title: China mandates sustainability reporting for index constituents
stories.summary: China’s securities exchanges now require companies in the SSE 180, STAR 50, Shenzhen 100, and ChiNext indices to disclose sustainability reports. Dual-listed companies must also comply. Covered firms are required to publicly disclose reports for the 2025 calendar year by 30 April 2027.

stories.title: Deloitte launches AI tool to detect greenwashing
stories.summary: Deloitte has unveiled the Green Claims Navigator, an artificial intelligence tool designed to identify misleading environmental statements in sustainability reports and marketing materials. The firm claims the software can vet claims within minutes. The tool is currently available across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

stories.title: KPMG discusses nature-related risk disclosures
stories.summary: KPMG’s latest episode of Corporate Reporting Today explores the International Sustainability Standards Board’s proposed practice statement on nature-related risks. The discussion focuses on location-specific analysis and the connections between nature and climate. The full piece is available for subscribers.

stories.title: ACCA report tracks Asia Pacific sustainability reporting
stories.summary: ACCA research finds that over 80% of ASEAN economies by GDP have adopted or plan to adopt International Sustainability Standards Board reporting standards. The report suggests that while the region leads in adoption, businesses must now translate these disclosures into long-term economic resilience and value.

stories.title: Tata Capital discloses SEBI settlement in sustainability report
stories.summary: Tata Capital Limited has filed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2025-26. The filing includes consolidated ESG metrics, such as 72,068.83 GJ of energy consumption, and discloses a ₹46.4 lakh settlement with the Securities and Exchange Board of India. The report was assured by SGS India.

stories.title: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank files sustainability report
stories.summary: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank has filed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2025-26. The document outlines environmental, social, and governance performance alongside operational efficiency metrics. The bank also disclosed monetary penalties totaling ₹45,03,750 imposed by various regulatory bodies during the financial year.

stories.title: MetroGAS uses AI to analyze sustainability report engagement
stories.summary: MetroGAS incorporated a virtual assistant into its 2025 Sustainability Report to track reader inquiries. The tool has received nearly 800 messages since its launch. The company says the data helps identify which topics generate the most interest and which sections require further explanation for readers.

stories.title: CaixaBank issues 1 billion euro green bond
stories.summary: CaixaBank has issued a five-year senior preferred green bond worth 1,000 million euros. The bank reported demand exceeding 4,500 million euros, marking the largest order book in its history for this type of instrument. The issuance followed a period of favorable conditions in credit and interest rate markets.

stories.title: Verra methodology receives carbon market approval
stories.summary: Verra has received approval from the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market for its methodology covering early coal plant retirement. The VM0052 standard allows transition credits to carry the Core Carbon Principles label. The organization expects the move to attract more investors to coal-to-renewable energy projects.

stories.title: Gabon sells 6 million forest carbon credits to SEFE
stories.summary: Gabon has agreed to sell 6 million metric tons of carbon dioxide credits to the German state-owned energy company SEFE. The credits are certified under the ART-TREES standard and are eligible for the aviation sector’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme. The deal was signed on 3 November 2026.

stories.title: Industry groups urge reform of Paris Agreement mechanisms
stories.summary: IETA, the Project Developer Forum, and the WCS have called for urgent guidance on Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement. The groups warn that complex baselines and high uncertainty requirements threaten the mechanism’s financial viability. They are requesting an official impact assessment of current standards to improve uptake.

stories.title: Outrigger Impact launches $100 million blue economy fund
stories.summary: Outrigger Impact has launched a fund targeting $100 million to provide equity and debt financing to businesses in Small Island Developing States. The firm aims to support 12,500 jobs and avoid 1 million tonnes of CO2 emissions. A final close for the fund is anticipated in 2027.

stories.title: Germany to purchase 6 million tons of carbon credits from Gabon
stories.summary: Gabon has agreed to sell 6 million tons of sovereign forest carbon credits to the German state-owned firm SEFE. The government describes the deal as Africa’s first sale of sovereign forest carbon credits. Proceeds will be held in a dedicated account pending a national distribution framework.

stories.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference has begun in Turkey, with a focus on implementing previous pledges to phase out coal, oil, and gas. Turkey is promoting an initiative to increase electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, driven by solar and wind.

stories.title: Pakistan official calls for national plastic waste framework
stories.summary: Minister of State for Climate Change Dr Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal has urged the government and private sector to develop a coordinated national framework for Extended Producer Responsibility. She said Pakistan needs to overhaul its waste management system and move towards a circular economy.

stories.title: Europe prepares Circular Economy Act
stories.summary: The European Commission is preparing to present the Circular Economy Act, a proposal intended to make circularity a lasting competitive advantage. Expected before the end of 2026, the initiative aims to keep materials in circulation and support investment in European recycling. The ambition includes permanent materials like steel.

stories.title: Achilles acquires contractor compliance platform Cm3
stories.summary: Achilles has completed its purchase of contractor management software provider Cm3 from the Blackwoods Group following approval from Australia’s Foreign Investment Review Board. The combined businesses now support more than 1,000 buying organisations. Cm3 will keep its established teams and services under the new ownership.

stories.title: GreenDot to acquire 50 percent of French recycler Léko
stories.summary: Agilyx subsidiary GreenDot has entered an agreement to acquire 50 percent of Valorie SAS, the parent company of French recycler Léko. GreenDot will share joint ownership with Reclay International. The transaction is funded from cash within the GreenDot Group.

stories.title: Retailers discard significant portions of returned stock
stories.summary: Research from ReBound Returns and Advanced Supply Chain finds half of retailers destroy or discard up to 40 percent of returned items. Only 27 percent of retailers divert most returns through circular routes. New EU regulations now include a ban on the destruction of certain unsold consumer goods.

stories.title: Somalia hosts first circular economy forum
stories.summary: Mogadishu hosted its first Circular Economy Forum to explore turning the city's 2,000 tonnes of daily waste into economic opportunities. Organized by Horn Thrive Hub, the event brought together environmental stakeholders and business leaders to discuss recycling initiatives. Waste is now being reconsidered as a potential resource.

stories.title: WRAP report links circular economy to job growth
stories.summary: A report from WRAP suggests that modest progress toward a circular economy could unlock nearly 4 billion pounds of additional value and 550,000 new jobs in the UK by 2035. The assessment examines the contribution of repair, reuse and leasing models to economic resilience.

stories.title: India proposes recycled plastic for food packaging
stories.summary: India is moving to allow wider use of recycled plastic in food packaging to help companies meet recycling targets. Under draft rules, recycled plastic must meet the same safety standards as new material. The proposal aims to remove a regulatory hurdle for the food industry.

stories.title: Jai Balaji Group announces steel and energy investment
stories.summary: Jai Balaji Group plans a 6,000 crore rupee investment in West Bengal for steel and renewable energy projects. The expansion is expected to generate 20,000 jobs. The company stated the project reflects confidence in the state's industrial potential and the new investment policy.

stories.title: India highlights renewable energy role at summit
stories.summary: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi stated that India has emerged as a major global force in renewable energy. Addressing the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit, he highlighted investor confidence and domestic manufacturing as key outcomes. The four-day event hosted participants from 135 countries and recorded 75,000 visitors.

stories.title: Ahold Delhaize hits renewable energy milestone
stories.summary: Ahold Delhaize has signed a 10-year virtual power purchase agreement with Rezolv Energy to support wind and solar projects in Romania. The retailer says it now matches its expected European electricity consumption with renewable sources by 2030, five years ahead of its original target.

stories.title: Tata Power commissions 300 MW solar project
stories.summary: Tata Power Renewable Energy has commissioned a 300 MW solar project in Karnataka for the Solar Energy Corporation of India. The facility is expected to produce 810 million units of electricity annually. The company says the project will prevent 103,820 tonnes of carbon emissions each year.

stories.title: India secures renewable energy investment commitments
stories.summary: India has secured $400 billion in renewable energy investment commitments, according to Union Minister Pralhad Joshi. The government previously saw ₹6 trillion to ₹7 trillion flow into the sector over two years. An additional ₹21 trillion is required by 2030 to reach the 500 gigawatt target.

stories.title: Green Genius raises $72.5 million via green bonds
stories.summary: Renewable energy developer Green Genius has completed a $72.5 million green bond issue to refinance construction loans. The bonds carry a floating interest rate based on the three month EURIBOR plus 8 percent. They are expected to trade on the Nasdaq Stockholm Sustainable Bond List.

stories.title: EgyptAlum signs 25 year solar deal to meet EU rules
stories.summary: Scatec has secured $217 million for its Dandara solar project in Egypt. The facility will provide power to the Aluminium Company of Egypt under a 25 year agreement. The project is designed to help the smelter comply with European Union carbon border adjustment requirements.

stories.title: Essar Power to build 300 MW project in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Essar Power will invest ₹4,500 crore to develop a 300 MW renewable energy project in Andhra Pradesh. The facility will combine solar and wind power with battery storage to provide dispatchable electricity. The company signed a power purchase agreement with state owned NHPC Ltd.

stories.title: India reports $400 billion in renewable investment interest
stories.summary: India received $400 billion in investment interest at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit, nearly double the amount estimated to be required by 2030. The government has not yet detailed the nature of these commitments or the specific companies involved. Interest is not always the same as investment.

stories.title: Indus Towers reaches 50,000 solar site milestone
stories.summary: Indus Towers has deployed 50,000 solar powered telecom sites across India, reaching a cumulative capacity of 300 MW. The company describes this as a global benchmark for sustainable infrastructure. It now aims to double its solar footprint to 100,000 sites.
